positions.name: Elastic N.V.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS GAPPER AND THE ONLY NEW 52-WEEK HIGH ON THE TAPE: Elastic reported FQ1 after the 8/27 close with revenue of $478.1M, up 15% year over year against a $469.8M consensus, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 versus a $0.44 estimate - a 59% surprise. The number that moved it was the guide: FY27 EPS of $3.29-$3.37 against a $2.64 street number, a 25-28% raise, plus operating cash flow of $132.0M and cash up to $881.8M. ESTC is +17.4% pre-market at 98.28 on a 98.20/98.75 book - a 0.56% spread - and that price is ABOVE the 96.065 52-week high set 11/12/2025. This is the only name in today's book breaking to new highs rather than bouncing inside a range.
positions.risks: THE ENTRY IS 17.4% ABOVE THE VERIFIED 83.74 CLOSE, WHICH BREACHES THE 15% PRE-PUBLISH BAND - I am taking it anyway because the price is confirmed by a live two-sided brokerage book at 06:19 CT, not inferred from a narrative, but it means we are paying the entire gap and have zero cushion. Elastic is a $8.7B company in the search/observability/SIEM market being squeezed from three directions at once - Datadog and Splunk above it, open-source OpenSearch below it - and the 15% revenue growth rate does not by itself justify a re-rating. A 17% gap on a mid-cap with a 2.38M-share 30-day average volume is thin enough that the open can be violent in either direction. Overnight only, deliberately.
positions.driver: Tier 1: earnings beat + large guidance raise

positions.name: Gap, Inc.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS GAPPER AT THE CHEAPEST MULTIPLE IN THE BOOK: Gap reported Q2 after the 8/27 close at $0.52 adjusted EPS on $3.7B of revenue and raised the full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $2.35-$2.45, up 10-15% year over year, on an improved gross margin outlook. It also named a new chief executive for Old Navy, its problem brand, and now guides Gap-brand comps to the high-single to low-double digits. GAP is +16.9% pre-market at 24.30 on a 24.25/24.64 book. It trades at 8.3x trailing earnings with a 3.2% dividend - by a wide margin the cheapest name in this book - and 8/27 volume of 22.9M ran 3.6x its 6.4M 30-day average.
positions.risks: THE ENTRY IS 16.9% ABOVE THE VERIFIED 20.79 CLOSE, ALSO OUTSIDE THE 15% BAND, and we closed this exact position at 20.79 last night for a -80 loss under the intraday rule - so we are buying our own stock back 17% higher, which is the identical mistake that cost 168 on Dollar General yesterday. The quarter itself was mixed: total sales FELL 2% year over year, and Old Navy - roughly half the company - was cut to flat-to-down-1% comps. The EPS raise is a gross-margin story, not a demand story. Old Navy CEO transitions at Gap have a poor track record. Overnight only, and the size is at the cap so there is no room to average.
positions.driver: Tier 1: earnings beat + raised FY guide + management change

positions.name: Affirm Holdings, Inc.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS GAPPER WITH THE TIGHTEST BOOK OF THE THREE: Affirm reported fiscal Q4 after the 8/27 close with revenue of $1.166B against a $1.128B consensus and raised the forward outlook - GMV of $49.27-$49.57B, revenue of $4.175-$4.205B and an adjusted operating margin of 28.2-28.8%. AFRM is +14.3% pre-market at 88.55 on an 88.50/88.70 book, a 0.23% spread on a $26B name, and the entry sits inside the 15% band. It is 11.5% below its 100.00 52-week high from 8/29/2025 and more than double its 42.10 low from 3/27.
positions.risks: THE EPS LINE IS GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS AND THAT IS A REAL RED FLAG: the verified earnings calendar records actual EPS of 0.48 against a 0.72 estimate - a MISS - while press coverage cites $4.62 versus $0.35. Those cannot both be the same measure, and it means the market is trading the revenue and GMV guide, not the bottom line. Buy-now-pay-later is the most credit-sensitive model we own and this is a fiscal year-end print, when charge-off and funding-cost disclosures get their fullest airing on the call - which happens after this entry. 69.5x earnings and 6.8x book. AFRM routinely moves 15-20% on earnings and has already moved 14% before we own it. Overnight only.

positions.name: Solstice Advanced Materials, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/1 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 CORPORATE ACTION, NOT AN EARNINGS TRADE - THE CLEANEST SETUP IN TODAY'S BOOK: On 8/27 Solstice and Element Solutions mutually terminated their planned acquisition, and the Solstice board simultaneously authorized a $500M share repurchase - 5.6% of the $8.95B market cap. SOLS is +13.7% pre-market at 64.08 on a 64.00/64.10 book, a TEN-CENT spread, the tightest quote of any new position. The market is plainly telling you it did not want the deal and does want the buyback. This is the Honeywell specialty-materials spinoff (refrigerants, semiconductor materials, data-center cooling, nuclear), completed 10/30/2025, and it is 29% below its 90.80 high from 5/13 - a broken-deal bounce off a de-rated base, not an extended chart.
positions.risks: THE BUSINESS ITSELF IS NOT WHY THIS IS UP AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM - Solstice guided full-year 2026 adjusted EPS to $2.45-$2.75 against a $2.93 consensus and sales to $3.9-$4.1B, citing higher operating costs, plant downtime and a messy transition to low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. Margins are under real pressure. A buyback pop on a company with deteriorating fundamentals typically has a short half-life, and 42.8x earnings is a rich multiple to pay for a chemicals business with those problems. This is also a ten-month-old public company with no long trading history to lean on and it just went ex-dividend on 8/27. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co.

The stock has gone from 65.45 (11/24/2025) to 154.58 in nine months, meaning most of the re-rating is behind us, and teen apparel is the single most fashion-cycle-dependent business in this book. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Dollar Tree, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/1 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 DAY-2 CONTINUATION AND THE ONLY RETAIL BEAT THAT DID NOT FAIL ITS GAP: Dollar Tree reported Q2 before the 8/27 open at $1.39 against a $1.03 estimate - a 35% surprise, the largest of the discount-retail cohort. What matters is the tape that followed: DLTR opened at 120.01, traded down to 118.11, then closed at 127.00, finishing +5.8% off its low and well above the open on 5.57M shares versus a 2.17M 30-day average. That is accumulation. Compare it to Dollar General and Burlington, which both gapped up on 8/27 and closed near their lows. DLTR is +0.9% again pre-market at the 127.20/129.09 midpoint of 128.15, at 16.1x earnings, and 10% below its 142.40 high from 1/15.
positions.risks: THE ENTRY IS A BID/ASK MIDPOINT, NOT A PRINT - the last actual pre-market trade was 127.86 at 02:20 CT and is stale, and the 1.5% spread means the mark is soft. This is also a day-2 entry, which means the easy money was made by people who owned it into the print; we are paying 0.9% above a close that already contains the beat. The trade-down consumer thesis that is working for DLTR is the same thesis that just cost this book 168 on Dollar General, and the two names are exposed to identical tariff and freight-cost pressure on imported general merchandise. Retail Trade is at the 4-name sector cap with GAP, ANF and BURL, so this book is heavily concentrated in one consumer bet. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: day-2 continuation on a 35% EPS surprise

positions.name: Rubrik, Inc.

Rubrik has NEGATIVE trailing earnings (P/E -73.7) and NEGATIVE book value (P/B -45.8), so there is no valuation floor under a $22B market cap whatsoever. It has gone from 42.25 (4/10) to 107.91 (8/27) in under five months, a 2.6x run, and a name that has doubled twice does not need a reason to give back 20%. Technology Services is at 2 names with ESTC, and both are software beats in a week where the market has repeatedly sold software beats - WDAY, ADSK, S and ULTA all beat and all traded down. Stop at -5%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: earnings beat, buying the after-hours give-back
